clue.text: Thoroughly acquainted with what poet wrote on day one

parts.note: a poet writes verse

indicators.note: the first letter, number one in order, of the word day

explanation.surface: A question of who knows the poet's work best, written up on the first day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' picks the first letter, D, of 'day'; 'on' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To be versed in something is to be skilled and knowledgeable about it.

clue.text: I enter two records before mid-January with energy at close of play

indicators.note: the letter I goes into the space between the two record words

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play gramophone record
a log is a written record, as a ship's log

indicators.note: the central letter of the seven-letter month name

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone logs a couple of discs in mid-January, finishing energetically as the game ends.
explanation.walkthrough: An EP is an extended-play disc; 'close of play' reads as cricket but means the end of a drama.
explanation.definitionFit: An epilogue is the closing speech or section of a drama, its final word after the action.

clue.text: Look over row, it is more revealing

parts.note: to scan is to look over quickly
a tier is a row, as of seats

explanation.surface: Checking a line of seats and finding one even more exposed.
explanation.definitionFit: Scantier clothing covers less, so it shows more of the body.

clue.text: Decide to put new timer in small valley

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit inside the valley word

parts.note: a dene is a small wooded valley

indicators.note: the letters of timer are made new, rearranged

explanation.surface: Instructions to fit a fresh clock somewhere in a little dale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to put' is a link; a dene is a mainly northern English word for a narrow valley.
explanation.definitionFit: To determine is to settle or resolve on a course of action.

clue.text: Two deserters back in charge of acid

indicators.note: the pair of deserter words are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a rat is one who deserts, as rats leave a sinking ship
the second deserter is another rat

explanation.surface: A pair of runaways come back to take command of something sour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns RATRAT into TARTAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Tartaric acid is the organic acid found in grapes and wine deposits.

clue.text: Persistent illegal parker at the station?

definitions.text: Persistent illegal parker at the station?

parts.words: Persistent illegal parker at the station?
parts.note: reads as a motorist who keeps collecting parking fines, but means the railway official who gathers passengers' travel passes

explanation.surface: A driver who keeps leaving the car where they shouldn't near the railway.
explanation.walkthrough: An illegal parker keeps getting tickets; the railway employee at the station takes them in.
explanation.definitionFit: This railway official checks and takes passengers' travel passes at the barrier.

clue.text: Excellent decapitation!

definitions.meaning: the slang act of cutting off someone's head

explanation.definitionFit: The word is informal for first-rate and also slang for executing by cutting off the head.

clue.text: Making short knocking sounds whilst talking briskly

explanation.definitionFit: Loose things clatter this way, and a fast talker rattles away at speed.

clue.text: Study never arranged by person summoning meeting

parts.note: to con is to study or learn carefully

indicators.note: the letters of never are set out in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone reviews the agenda set out by the chair calling a committee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' makes VENER from NEVER; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A convener is the organiser who calls members together to assemble.

clue.text: Vast grotesque carriage in the lead

indicators.note: the carriage word goes at the front, ahead of the grotesque word

parts.note: a gig is a light two-wheeled horse carriage
antic as an adjective means grotesque or bizarre

explanation.surface: A huge, bizarre horse-drawn vehicle heads the procession.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue lists the grotesque word before the carriage, so 'in the lead' is needed to reverse their order.
explanation.definitionFit: Gigantic means enormous, of giant size.

clue.text: Absolutely correct, place has no backing

parts.note: a spot is a place

indicators.note: the word no is given in reverse, backed up

explanation.surface: A venue that lacks financial support is just right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns NO into ON; 'has' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Spot-on is a British idiom for exactly right.

clue.text: Situation vacant — and no stamp needed when applying

parts.note: a post is a job, a situation
free means unoccupied

explanation.surface: A job advert says apply without paying for postage.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like a job application; the definition is about a letter going without postage paid.
explanation.definitionFit: Mail sent post-free needs no paid postage from the sender.

clue.text: Highland attendant's girl not right to be dishonest

definitions.note: attendant's here stands for attendant is

indicators.note: the letter R, for right, is dropped from the girl word

parts.note: taken as written
to lie is to be dishonest

explanation.surface: A Scottish servant's girlfriend proves untrustworthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not right' removes R from GIRL to leave GIL. The 's of the definition reads as is.
explanation.definitionFit: A gillie is a hunting or fishing guide and servant on a Scottish estate.

clue.text: Showing clearly it was gin cocktail vince mixed first

indicators.note: the mixed name comes at the front, ahead of the gin letters
the letters of vince are mixed into a new order
the letters of gin are shaken up like a cocktail

explanation.surface: A drinker called Vince reveals what was in his drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Two anagram signals work on separate words; 'it was' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To evince is to display or make evident a quality.

clue.text: Coming from Inverness with timidity

indicators.note: the letters are reshaped, the answer emerging out of the town name

explanation.surface: A shy visitor arrives from a Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: INVERNESS is a city in the Scottish Highlands; its letters rearrange exactly.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerviness is nervousness, a jumpy lack of confidence.

clue.text: Ne flower show

definitions.meaning: a river of north-east England, flower read as something that flows

explanation.definitionFit: The Wear flows through Durham and Sunderland; to wear is also to exhibit.

clue.text: One entering path to win with ease

indicators.note: the single letter goes into the path word

parts.note: a walkway is a path
A, the indefinite article, means one

explanation.surface: A runner enters the track and cruises to victory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entering' puts A inside WALKWAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A walkaway is a contest won easily, a stroll to victory.

clue.text: Lively one I beat on board

parts.note: one gives AN
in chess, to be mated is to be beaten by checkmate

explanation.surface: A player cheerfully reports winning a game of chess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beat on board' refers to checkmate in chess.
explanation.definitionFit: Animated means full of life and spirit.

clue.text: A fish jelly

parts.note: a gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: A fish set in aspic.
explanation.definitionFit: Agar is a gelatinous substance from seaweed used as a setting agent.

clue.text: Put together measure that's pronouncedly stupid at the end

definitions.note: an adverbial phrase standing for a thing tacked on at the close

parts.note: to add is to put together
an en is a printer's measure

indicators.note: the word for stupid is spoken, giving its sound only

parts.note: dumb means stupid

explanation.surface: Combining units that sound silly in the last part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pronouncedly' signals DUMB said aloud, written DUM. The definition is loose: an addendum is something placed at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: An addendum is a supplement appended to the close of a book or document.

clue.text: Constrictor from Canada on form

indicators.note: the letters are put into a new shape or form

explanation.surface: A big snake turns up from Canada in good shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' rearranges CANADA plus ON; 'from' links.
explanation.definitionFit: The anaconda is a huge South American snake that kills by squeezing.

clue.text: Brought up after spring having good manners

indicators.note: the brought-up word comes after the spring word

parts.note: a well is a spring of water
bred means raised or reared

explanation.surface: A child raised after springtime turns out polite.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a child raised after springtime; 'spring' is the water source.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone well-bred was raised to be courteous and refined.

clue.text: Idler Walter's confused

indicators.note: the letters of the name are muddled

parts.note: the name with its possessive s kept as a letter

explanation.surface: Walter is a lazy man in a muddle.
explanation.walkthrough: Here the 's counts as a letter: WALTERS rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A wastrel is a good-for-nothing who squanders time and money.

clue.text: Hesitantly inside touch mares' milk that has fermented

indicators.note: the hesitation sound goes inside the touch word

parts.note: a kiss is a light touch
um is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A nervous peck shared over a glass of fermented horse milk.
explanation.walkthrough: Kumiss is drunk across the Central Asian steppe.
explanation.definitionFit: Kumiss is a Central Asian drink made by fermenting horse milk.

clue.text: Without a single piece of information on church in distress

parts.note: ex means without, as in ex dividend
I is the Roman numeral one
gen is British slang for information
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone with no news at all about the church is in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' and 'in' are links; GEN is British informal for information.
explanation.definitionFit: Exigence is an urgent need or pressing difficulty.

clue.text: Tearful when tasteless

definitions.meaning: weak and diluted, as thin soup

explanation.definitionFit: Watery eyes are moist with tears; watery food is bland and diluted.

clue.text: Putting one's foot down

parts.note: reads as being firm, but means literally setting one's sole on the ground in walking

explanation.definitionFit: Treading is stepping, placing the feet as one walks.

clue.text: Highly unnatural singer

parts.note: an Alpine vocalist who flips abruptly into falsetto, singing high in an artificial voice

explanation.definitionFit: This Alpine vocal style switches rapidly between chest voice and falsetto.

clue.text: Missile Peter found on boat

parts.note: SAM is a surface-to-air missile
Peter Pan, the boy who never grew up

explanation.surface: Peter turns up on a vessel armed with a rocket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found on' links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A sampan is a small flat-bottomed boat of East Asia.
